To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proteome of Cu-stressed rice roots contains proteins that play an important role, in the detoxification and tolerance of excess Cu, and that these proteins differ between a Cu-tolerant rice variety and a Cu-sensitive rice variety.

the Cu-toleran variety B1139 showed higher Cu-binding protein expression levels than the Cu-sensitive variety, B1195, in Cu-stressed roots, suggesting that these proteins play an important role for the detoxification of Cu and for maintaining cellular homeostatic balance in Cu-stressed rice.

the Cu-binding proteome of rice roots was successfully identified using the IDA-sephareos-Cu-IMAC method, and that Cu-binding proteins involved in the detoxification and homeostasis of Cu, and the regulation of gene expression and protein synthesis, modification and degradation were up-regulated in the tolerant variety.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of proteins involved in Cu stress tolerance and the development of new methods for studying metal binding proteins in plants.
the identification of Cu-binding proteins and the elucidation of their roles in Cu stress responses in rice.
the identification of the Cu-binding protein profiles in rice varieties under Cu stress and provides new insights into the mechanisms of Cu tolerance in rice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Cu-binding proteins, which are differentially expressed in the Cu-tolerance and Cu-sensitivity rice varieties, may be involved in Cu detoxification, and in the Cu-treatment induced stress responses and tolerance.
the Cu-binding proteins identified in this study may play an important role, directly or indirectly, in the Cu tolerance mechanism of rice.

the Cu-tolerable rice variety has more Cu-binding proteins and more Cu-responsive proteins, including those involved in antioxidant defenses and detoxification, pathogenesis, regulation of gene transcription, amino acid synthesis, protein synthesis, modification and degradation, cell wall synthesis, molecular signaling, and salt stress, than the Cu-sensitive rice variety.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Cu-responsive proteins are involved in the detoxification and tolerance of excess Cu, and the differences in the Cu-responsive proteins between the two rice varieties are related to their different Cu tolerances.
Cu-tolerant rice plants are able to tolerate Cu stress through up-regulating Cu-binding proteins and related physiological processes, which are involved in the detoxification and homeostasis of Cu.

the Cu-toleran rice variety, B1139, has a more effective mechanism for Cu detoxification and homeostasis, which is associated with a more active antioxidant system and the induction of a number of proteins involved in detoxification, transport, degradation and modification of Cu-binding proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Cu-toleran variety, B1139, has the ability to maintain cellular homeostasis by up-regulating the antioxidant system, detoxification, protein synthesis and degradation, and other processes, while the Cu-sensitive variety, B1195, has the ability of down-regulating these systems to reduce the damage caused by Cu stress.
Cu-binding proteins are involved in the detoxification and homeostasis of excess Cu in plants, and that these proteins are differentially expressed in Cu-tolerants and Cu-sensitive rice cultivars.
Cu-binding proteins play an important role during Cu stress and tolerance in rice.
